svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.23.6.1 Anchorage of Building Frames
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.23 WOOD-FRAME CONSTRUCTION
Anchorage of Building Frames

g.text: Anchor bolts not less than 12.7 mm, with
Embedded not less than 100 mm, able to be
Or: ends of the first floor joists embedded
Sill plate anchored to the foundation
Braced wall panel, Smax for Site Class C
At least two bolts, at opposite ends, then
Anchor bolts in a braced wall panel
TABLE 9.23.6.1., ANCHOR BOLT SPACING WITHIN BRACED WALL PANELS, M
Where HWP ≤ 1.2 kPa, Smax for Site Class C > 0.47 and Smax ≤ 2.6
Reference framing types are those of Table 9.23.3.5.-C. Table shown with its rows and columns swapped.
Sentence (3) says "except as provided in Sentence (6)", but no Sentence (6) is printed in this Article.

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except as required by Sentence 9.23.6.3.(1), building
frames are anchored to the foundation unless a
structural analysis of wind and earthquake loads and
lateral earth pressures shows it is not required.
Except as provided in Sentences (3) to (5), anchorage is
by
(a) embedding the ends of the first floor joists in
concrete, or (b) fastening the sill plate to the foundation
with anchor bolts not less than 12.7 mm in diameter, spaced
not more than 2.4 m o.c.
Where Smax for Site Class C is over 0.47, braced wall
panels are anchored with anchor bolts through the sill
plate,
(a) at least two per panel, at opposite ends, within 0.5 m
of the foundation end or within 0.3 m of the panel end, and
(b) spaced to Table 9.23.6.1.
These anchor bolts are fastened to the sill plate with
nuts and washers, embedded not less than 100 mm in the
foundation, and able to be tightened without withdrawing
them.
Anchorage is designed to Part 4 where the HWP is over
1.2 kPa, Smax is over 2.6, or Smax for Site Class C is
over 0.47 for 3-storey buildings of heavy weight
construction, or clad at full height with masonry veneer
or with "some stone veneer" (as printed).
Drawn: bolts at the minimum count, nuts and washers grey. Sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.6.1. (page 9-176)
